newsitem.title: UK: UK PEP investment growing at 70 pct rate - study.
newsitem.headline: UK PEP investment growing at 70 pct rate - study.

text.p: British retail investment in Personal Equity Plans (PEPs) has risen at an average rate of 70 percent over the past five years, far outstripping other forms of investment, according to a study by Datamonitor.
Datamonitor said that funds under management in PEPs rose to 25 billion stg in 1996 from three billion in 1992.
Unit trust also experienced strong growth, rising to 132 billion stg from 64 billion stg in the same period, an annual rate of 20 percent.
Investment trusts have also grown, but at the slightly slower rate of 17 percent annually.
Much of the growth is due to a desire to earn better returns in equity investments, according to the report from the research group.

"People are seeing the great returns in the stock market and seeking to capitalise. The buoyant markets in 1996 had a great effect (on equity inflows)," said Caroline Sahakian, an analyst at Datamonitor.
Investment in bank and building societies increased as well, Datamonitor said, but grew at an annual rate of only five percent in the period.
Collective investment vehicles, such as PEPs and unit trusts, will overtake direct forms of investment, such as shareholding, between now and the year 2000, according to Datamonitor.
"There are many factors which explain this, the most important are: lower costs and charges, the opportunity to spread risk, and extensive product choice," Sahakian said.
"In addition, the demutualisations and the resulting windfall shares awarded to individuals in 1997, should further increase the flow of funds."
Direct equity investment is forecast to have a net outflow of funds between 1996 and 2000, with unit trusts, investment trusts and PEPs the main beneficiaries, according to the survey.
Datamonitor produced the survey based on an analysis of industry and government databases as well as a survey of investment managers and professionals.
